result.title: D-REAL: Acceptance-Length Optimization with Unbiased Gradients for Speculative Decoding
result.summary: Speculative decoding efficiency depends on the number of consecutively accepted draft tokens, yet token-level training objectives do not directly optimize this quantity. We introduce D-REAL (Drafter Reinforcement of Expected Acceptance Length), a post-training method that directly optimizes expected acceptance length for a fixed decoding context. D-REAL weights position-wise draft-target distributional overlap by prefix survival probabilities along a draft-sampled prefix, faithfully capturing the sequential dependence of verification on earlier proposals. By accounting for the parameter dependence of the proposal distribution, we derive an unbiased gradient estimator for this single-round objective under stochastic verification. We evaluate D-REAL on DSpark and DFlash2 with Qwen3-8B as the target model across ten benchmarks. Starting from baselines whose mean acceptance length has plateaued, one epoch of D-REAL post-training consistently improves the benchmark-averaged mean acceptance length by up to 0.23 tokens across both architectures under greedy (T = 0.0) and stochastic (T = 1.0) sampling, translating into up to a 9.4% end-to-end serving throughput improvement.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 D-REAL，一种投机解码 draft 模型的后训练方法：直接优化固定解码上下文下的期望接受长度，按草稿前缀存活概率对各位置的 draft-target 分布重叠加权，并为随机验证下的单轮目标推导无偏梯度估计器，在 Qwen3-8B 等设定上提升平均接受长度与端到端吞吐。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理，但「以前缀存活概率为各位置分配训练信号、对序列级目标构造无偏梯度估计」的思路，可能为 latent 多步推理中早期状态对后续验证的贡献分配与监督提供可核查的方法线索。
